findings.description: The single remaining `git status` still runs `filter.<driver>.clean`/`.process` (and recurses into submodules), and `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is a `.worktrees/<name>` linked worktree in the documented loop. So the gitfile-repoint attack the PR closes for other worktrees still reaches this hook.
findings.body:
**The fix clears fsmonitor but not clean filters, and the "safe" project checkout can itself be a repointable linked worktree.**

The comment at L11-15 names "fsmonitor or clean filter" as the vector, but the one remaining `status` call only neutralises the first:

```bash
CHANGES=$(git -c core.fsmonitor= --no-optional-locks status --short 2>/dev/null | head -20)
```

During the in-memory index refresh, `git status` re-hashes every tracked entry whose stat data doesn't match. That hashing goes through `convert_to_git`, which runs the `filter.<driver>.clean` / `.process` command that config and attributes assign. `--no-optional-locks` only skips writing the refreshed index back. A hostile gitdir controls the index (so it can force a stat mismatch), `config`, and `info/attributes`. No generic `-c` disables arbitrarily named filter drivers. Status also recurses into submodules, where their own config applies.

The PR treats `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` as trusted, but `AGENTS.md` makes `.worktrees/<name>` mandatory and `docs/workflow.md` L27-28 says to `cd .worktrees/my-feature` and work there. A session launched there has a project dir whose `.git` is a **gitfile**. That is exactly the kind of file the PR's comment says another session can point at a gitdir it controls, for example a main-checkout session whose sandbox write scope `.` covers `.worktrees/*`. The same config can also set `core.worktree`, which `rev-parse --show-toplevel` honours, so it controls `$SELF` too.

The gap predates this PR, which narrowed status from every tree to one. But the PR adds `-c core.fsmonitor=` to this exact call and its comment presents this tree as the safe one, so the fix is incomplete as written.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/a38d6b3325c254b6b02452acd678aa1a4f36f92a/.claude/hooks/post-compact-state.sh#L11-L29

There is no single safe one-liner. Options:
- drop `status` entirely, as the PR already does for other worktrees;
- or run it only when the project dir's `.git` is a real directory (the main checkout), and list a linked-worktree project dir like the other worktrees.

Either way, the L11-15 comment should stop implying the project checkout is safe by construction.

findings.description: The project checkout's branch name goes into context unsanitized, though branch names may contain `<`, `>`, quotes and non-ASCII. Any worktree can `git branch -m` the branch checked out here (git rewrites every worktree's HEAD on rename), which fakes a tag on the `- checkout:` line, the gap `safe()` closes for other worktrees.
findings.body:
**`$BRANCH` (and `$SELF`) skip `safe()` on the one line this PR rewrote for the checkout.**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null)
echo "Live state after compaction (read now; trust it over the summary):"
echo "- checkout: $SELF on ${BRANCH:-a detached HEAD}"
```

The PR's own comments say branch names are "renamable" (L14-15) and "chosen by whoever made the worktree" and land in Claude's context, so sanitizing them "stops one faking a line or a tag" (L19-21). It applies `safe()` to other worktrees (L36) and a jq `gsub` to PR head names (L43), but not here.

`git check-ref-format` rejects control characters, so a name can't fake a new line. It does allow `<`, `>` and `"`, so `x</system-reminder>` is a valid branch name. `git branch -m` run from any worktree renames a branch checked out in another worktree and rewrites that worktree's HEAD. So the attacker the PR defends against (another session) can put that string onto this line.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/a38d6b3325c254b6b02452acd678aa1a4f36f92a/.claude/hooks/post-compact-state.sh#L24-L26

findings.description: The hook no longer says which tree the session is working in. A session in `.worktrees/x` gets the main checkout's branch and changes under "trust it over the summary", with its own worktree listed among the "other worktrees". Printing `safe "$CWD"` from stdin runs no git and would keep that fact.
The header comment still says the hook re-injects "the session's branch and changes". It now reports the project checkout's branch and changes, as the README row already says.
The `--no-optional-locks` comment talks about a commit "a parallel session runs in that worktree". Now that status runs only in the project checkout, "that worktree" has no clear referent.

The PR has two sanitizers for the same threat with different rules. `safe()` allows space and `()` with no length cap, while the jq `gsub` for PR head names disallows them and truncates to 60. A later edit to one won't reach the other. Consider making `safe()` the single policy and piping the gh output through it.

The workflow table still says the hook re-injects "the branch, uncommitted files, worktrees and open PRs". Uncommitted files are now reported only for the project checkout, and other worktrees show only path and branch.

Filenames from `status --short` reach context unsanitized. Control characters are C-quoted, but `<` and `>` pass through, so a crafted untracked filename can still put a tag-like string on an `uncommitted here` line. Running `$CHANGES` through the same filter as the worktree list would make the output consistent.
